hard_gates.evidence: I extended r17's script with B's contacts, custom fields and attachments (attack/attack.mjs, attack-run.log). It sent 245 operations with B's ids, 1,648 documented query-parameter requests, 1,050 tenant-switch requests (headers, query, cookies), 190 export requests, 77 filter requests (contacts and audit log added) and 328 path-form, audit-record and attachment requests. B's rows in every tenant table were the same before and after (b-before/b-after; a re-check after the attacker's queued job ran showed no difference either). I triaged all 137 flagged lines and none is a leak (attack/probe.txt). (1) 'الخليج' and 'Gulf Steel' come from A's own seeded contacts: 1,633 and 143 rows in alnoor, e.g. 'Gulf Steel Industries FZCO'. (2) B's tenant id appears in A's audit log only inside a payload A itself sent: a jobs.cleanup job and schedule. That job ran in tenant A and B was unchanged. (3) The 81 answers from /api/audit/records with B's ids are byte-identical to the answer for a random id, apart from the trace id. (4) DELETE of B's attachment answered 204 as a no-op: B still downloads its 601-byte file and A gets 404. (5) DELETE of B's rate answered 204 as a no-op, the same as since r15: B still sees it and A gets 404.

biggest_gap.title: The gate suite takes 3 h 14 min on a quiet machine, and the processor-time ratchet sees only about a third of the CPU it uses
biggest_gap.detail: Every gate held and every test passed. The cost of proving it is what now holds the foundation back. The verify ran alone through the slot script with nothing else heavy running, and still took 11,656 s of wall time. The ratchet's own target for a quiet machine is 3,600 s. G1HttpIsolationTests alone took 2 h 40 m, and the dotnet stage took 10,374 s. Processor time was 19,648 s against the 20,800 s maximum. That leaves about 1,150 s of headroom, so the next new piece's first integration will need the maximum raised again. That figure is also only part of the real cost. Over the same run the machine used 55,057 processor seconds, and the ratchet counted 35,409 s of it (64.3 %) as 'other work beside the verify'. build/verify-inside.sh documents that the PostgreSQL containers the tests start, the verify stack's containers and the image build are not counted. During the dotnet stage I saw a Testcontainers PostgreSQL container ('blissful_jang') running at 90 to 160 % CPU while the toolbox container held 4.5 to 5.9 GB. So the number the owner's ratchet watches grows more slowly than the real cost per new endpoint. Each critic and integrator round already needs more than 3 hours of exclusive machine time, which slows every later piece's loop. Builders need either a cheaper per-endpoint attack (G1HttpIsolation) or a ratchet line that also counts the test databases.
biggest_gap.evidence: verify-critic-p00-foundation-r19.log: 'verify passed in 11656 s'; 'stage dotnet passed in 10374 s'; 'Passed Erp.Gates.Tests.G1.G1HttpIsolationTests.Tenant_A_cannot_reach_tenant_B_through_any_endpoint [2 h 40 m]'. ratchet-check.txt: 'verify processor time: 19648 s (... maximum 20800 s)'; 'machine processor time over the run: 55057 s; verify stages 19648 s; other work beside the verify 35409 s (64.3 % of the machine's)'; 'maximum on a quiet machine 3600 s; not judged'. The not-counted containers are named in build/verify-inside.sh lines 18-20. To reproduce, run the same verify command alone on a quiet machine and read the [ratchet] lines.

other_findings: No gate gap this round. All three live plants were caught: L19 (a cross-tenant memo of deep-page totals), P19 (an implied read permission in HasPermission) and P17 (the trailing-slash bypass, backlog row 15). Row 15 was missed in r17 and is now caught by G2PathCaseTests, so it can be closed. Details in plants/plant-results.txt.

Strength: erp_app is refused the statistics views ('42501: permission denied for view pg_stat_user_tables') and pg_class's estimate columns, so a 'fast count from statistics' leak cannot even run (plants/l19-pgstat-error.txt; KernelSql.RevokeCrossTenantStatistics).

G1NonInterferenceTests passed with L19 on: it asks no deep page. Two other gates caught L19 (G1ProcessStateTests statically, G1ListVolumeTests dynamically), so this is not a gap, only a note on which gate covers which window.

The serial-19 and r17 failures hold in this quiet alone run: G1CompanyIsolationTests (10 m 16 s), G1ListVolumeTests at demo volume (19 m 50 s) and the GateSelfTests HTTP-attack planted-leak test all passed. The new paging rule in G1CompanyIsolation (take/skip answers judged by shape and totals only, rows still searched for markers) hides no real fault I found. By design it would not notice a company-Y oracle that changes only which rows a paging window shows, without any marker.
